arianism.summary: The Church teaches that the Son is begotten, not made. He is of one being with the Father, eternal, and truly God. Only if the one who became man is himself God can he save us, be worshipped, and be the Creator of all things.

steps.0: The Word was with God and was God.
steps.1: Paul says the Son is before all things and all things were made through him.
steps.2: The Son is to be honoured as the Father is. Giving that to a creature would be wrong.
steps.3: Athanasius says the Son is the Father’s own offspring, not something made.
steps.4: Athanasius says that if the Son is not truly God, the whole argument with others is lost.
steps.5: Only the Creator could make people new again.
steps.6: The Incarnation is to share God’s life with us. Only God can do that.
steps.7: Nicaea says “begotten, not made” and “of one being”.
steps.8: The council’s letter tells the churches which Arian teachings it rejected.

objections: Athanasius does not deny the Greek Bible says “created” here. He spends a long time on this verse. The Hebrew word means “possessed” or “acquired”, which is not the same as “made”.
The Fathers read such words as spoken about the Son as a man, in the form of a servant. Words like “I and the Father are one” speak of his divine nature.
No. The Church rejects that mistake too. The Persons are really distinct and share one divine nature.

gnosticism-docetism.summary: The Church teaches that the Word truly became flesh. He was born of Mary, really suffered and rose. The body is God’s good creation and is meant to rise. Salvation is not escaping matter. It is healing it.

steps.0: The Word did not just appear in flesh. He became flesh.
steps.1: John says confessing that Jesus came in the flesh is the test of the Spirit.
steps.2: The risen Christ insists on his body.
steps.3: Ignatius says that if the Cross were only appearance, his own chains and death would mean nothing.
steps.4: Without real suffering there is no love shown.
steps.5: Redemption needs him to share our real nature.
steps.6: If flesh cannot be saved, the Eucharist loses its meaning.
steps.7: The Catechism: creation, Incarnation and resurrection all honour the body.

objections: Irenaeus takes this very verse. Flesh without the Spirit is dead. The body is saved when the Spirit gives it life. Paul says in the same chapter that the perishable will put on what does not perish.
Irenaeus says the apostles’ teaching was open. Anyone can trace the churches they founded and the bishops after them. Secret teachings for a few would not fit.
The Bible says God made the body and called it good. Sin is the problem, not matter. In Christ, God healed what he made.

marcionism.summary: The Church teaches there is one God who made heaven and earth, spoke through the Law and the Prophets, and sent his Son. The Old Testament is the Church’s own Scripture, read in the light of Christ. He came not to destroy but to fulfil.

steps.0: Jesus calls his Father “Lord of heaven and earth”.
steps.1: Jesus says he came to fulfil the Law and the Prophets.
steps.2: Even Paul says the Gospel was promised through the prophets.
steps.3: Irenaeus says a God who is not good is no God, and goodness needs justice.
steps.4: Irenaeus says the “unknown God” is described in great detail by those who say he is unknown.
steps.5: Tertullian says a god who only forbids sin in words gives no reason to fear it.
steps.6: The Creed starts with one God, Father and Creator.
steps.7: The Catechism names this view and refuses it.

objections: The Old Testament calls God merciful and gracious before it calls him judge. The New Testament also warns of judgment. Irenaeus says to read both the Gospel and the prophets with care.
Paul himself calls the Law holy, righteous and good. Irenaeus says the same God worked through Peter and through Paul.
Irenaeus says picking the parts of Luke one likes is arbitrary. The Church received the Gospels from the apostles and their successors.

modalism-sabellianism.summary: The Church teaches one God in three distinct Persons. The Father is not the Son and the Son is not the Spirit. All three share one divine nature. It was the Son, not the Father, who became man, suffered and died.

steps.0: At Jesus’ baptism the Son is in the water, the Spirit comes down, and the Father speaks.
steps.1: Jesus speaks to the Father as another, and of shared glory before the world.
steps.2: The Son prays, the Father gives, and the Spirit is called another Counselor.
steps.3: Baptism is in one name, with three Persons named.
steps.4: Tertullian says the three are distinct but not separate.
steps.5: Tertullian refuses the idea that the Father suffered. The Son died.
steps.6: Tertullian says God’s unity is believed in a new way, through the Son.
steps.7: Hippolytus says Scripture shows three, while God is one.
steps.8: The Catechism says the names are not just modes of one Person.

objections: Not for the writers who answered Noetus and Praxeas. They held one God. They said the Word is God with the Father. John’s opening words already hold both the unity and the difference.
The same Gospel says “I am in the Father, and the Father in me”, which already speaks of two. The Greek says “we are one thing”. That is different from “I am the Father”.

nestorianism.summary: The Church teaches that Jesus Christ is one Person, the eternal Son of God, who took a human nature as his own. Mary is called Mother of God because the one she bore is God the Son. This does not mean she is the source of his divinity.

steps.0: Elizabeth calls Mary the mother of her Lord.
steps.1: The one sent by God is the one born of a woman.
steps.3: The one crucified is called Lord of glory.
steps.4: Cyril says calling Mary Theotokos does not make her the source of the Word.
steps.5: Cyril says the natures stay different even though the Person is one.
steps.6: One Christ, not a man and a God sharing a title.
steps.7: Cyril’s first anathema puts the point in one sentence. These were Cyril’s own words.
steps.8: Ephesus judged that the new teaching undermines the Incarnation.
steps.9: The Catechism: the one who has the humanity is the Son of God.

objections: The worry is understandable, and Cyril shared it. He says the title does not mean God’s nature began in Mary. It means the one she bore in the flesh is the eternal Word.
The Church never said the divine nature suffers in itself. She says the Son of God suffered in the flesh he made his own. Paul speaks of the Lord of glory crucified.
The Church rejected that too, at Chalcedon. Cyril himself spoke of a union of two natures. The difference stays.

monophysitism-eutychianism.summary: The Church teaches that Christ is one Person in two natures, God and man, “without confusion, change, division or separation”. He is of one being with the Father in his Godhead, and with us in his manhood.

steps.0: John says confessing a real human nature is part of the test of faith.
steps.1: The risen Lord still has a body that can be touched.
steps.2: To be our high priest he had to be like us in all things.
steps.3: Both “forms” are named in one subject.
steps.4: Leo: two natures kept, one Person.
steps.5: Leo: the wounds and touch show both natures are real.
steps.6: Leo: the Passion is real because the flesh is real.
steps.7: Chalcedon states both ways in which Christ is like us and like the Father.
steps.8: The Catechism quotes the four negatives of Chalcedon.

objections: The unity of Christ is in the Person. Cyril, who stood for unity, spoke of a union of two natures and one Christ. The council did not reject unity. It rejected mixing.
Chalcedon rejects that division in the same sentence. It says “one and the same” Son, in two natures. Ephesus had already rejected splitting Christ into a man and a God.
Leo says suffering belongs to the Person, through the nature that can suffer. The same Christ can die in one nature and not in the other. So the Son truly suffers and the Godhead is not changed.

pelagianism.summary: The Church teaches that Adam’s sin wounded the whole human race. No one can begin, go on or finish the way of salvation without God’s grace first. Free will is real and not destroyed. It is healed and carried forward by grace. Grace is a gift, never a wage.

steps.0: Paul says sin and death came to all through one man.
steps.1: Christ says no fruit comes without him.
steps.2: Augustine says the will is free, and is moved to love the good by God’s gift.
steps.3: Augustine says sin can be avoided. How? By nature healed, not nature alone.
steps.4: Augustine’s prayer shows what he always believed: God gives what he commands.
steps.5: Trent rejects the claim about Adam.
steps.6: Trent says no one is justified by his own works apart from grace.
steps.7: The Catechism names the error and how Orange and Trent answered it.
steps.8: Even the first step toward God is God’s gift.

objections: Augustine says the ability was lost through a wound, not by God’s plan. A healer restores it. A man is rightly told he should not be lame, even if he cannot cure himself by wishing.
No. The Church rejects that mistake as firmly. Grace moves the will without forcing it. A person really agrees and really works with God. He could refuse.
The Church does not say a baby has done wrong. Original sin is a lack of the holiness human nature was meant to have. It is passed on by birth. Baptism restores it.

donatism.summary: The Church teaches that Christ himself is the true giver of every sacrament. A valid baptism or ordination does not depend on how holy the minister is. The Church on earth is a mixed body of saints and sinners until the harvest. Splitting the Church to be pure is itself a serious wrong.

steps.0: Christ tells the servants not to pull the weeds before harvest.
steps.1: The real baptiser is Christ, whoever pours the water.
steps.2: Paul rebukes people who tie baptism to a minister’s name.
steps.3: Cyprian condemns the pride of those who try to purge the Church before judgment.
steps.4: Augustine says baptism is Christ’s and the Church’s. It does not belong to a group.
steps.5: Augustine says on the Donatist view no one could be sure his baptism was real.
steps.6: The mixture of good and bad is real but lasts only for a time.
steps.7: Cyprian says leaving the Church breaks unity.
steps.8: The Catechism says the sacrament works by Christ’s act.
steps.9: The Church is holy by Christ’s life in her, even though her members are sinners.

objections: Cyprian did hold that view, and Augustine says so. But Cyprian refused to break communion over it. The whole Church settled it later. The Donatists kept his opinion and dropped his peace.
Paul wrote to the Corinthians as a Church although they had faults. He told them to correct offenders, not leave the Church. Cyprian himself stayed in communion with those who disagreed.

It is a fair criticism, and the Church does not pretend otherwise. Augustine first opposed force. After Donatist violence he accepted pressure from the emperor. The Church today regrets the use of force in matters of faith.

manichaeism.summary: The Church teaches there is one God, who made all things seen and unseen. Everything he made is good. Evil is not a rival thing. It is the lack of a good that should be there. It enters the world when creatures misuse freedom. The Word became flesh, so the body and the material world are good.

steps.0: The Bible’s first page says all created things are good.
steps.1: Everything was made through Christ, so there is no second creator.
steps.2: If the Word took flesh, flesh cannot be the work of God’s enemy.
steps.3: Paul says forbidding marriage and some foods is a mark of false teaching.
steps.4: The first creed confesses one God, maker of all.
steps.5: Augustine says the Manichaean system makes God able to be harmed.
steps.6: Augustine says first ask what evil is.
steps.7: From his own life Augustine says evil is the lack of good, not a thing.
steps.8: Every real being is good as far as it exists. Evil is falling away from being.
steps.9: The Catechism repeats that creation is good.

objections: It is the easiest answer to say, and Augustine admits it first drew him in. But it limits God and cannot explain how a second power could exist. The Church says evil is the lack of a good.
The Church honours fasting and celibacy as free gifts for growth, never as rejecting the body. Augustine insists marriage and children are good.
Augustine felt this and says so. What changed his mind was hearing Ambrose explain such passages as a figure. The difficulty is real, but there is an answer.

novatianism-rigorism.summary: The Church teaches that Christ gave her the power to forgive all sins. No one who is sorry is turned away, however big the fall. Penance can be hard and long, but it leads to making peace. To refuse forgiveness altogether is to deny the keys Christ gave.

steps.0: The risen Christ gives the apostles power to forgive and to hold back sins.
steps.1: The power of binding and loosing is given to the Church. Loosing is part of it.
steps.2: Paul tells Corinth to take back a sinner who had been disciplined.
steps.3: Cyprian was strict, but insists on a middle way between harshness and softness.
steps.4: Refusing peace to the sorry makes repentance pointless and leads to despair.
steps.5: Ambrose says a Church that binds but never looses has misread Christ.
steps.6: Nicaea requires returning Cathari to accept the Church’s practice of pardoning.
steps.7: The Catechism says the keys reach every sorry sinner.
steps.8: The Church asks serious penance for serious sin. She never closes the door.

objections: Ambrose gave two answers. The passage is about not being baptised a second time, since there is one baptism. And what is impossible for people is possible for God.
Cyprian rejected this. The strength of the faithful does not depend on shutting the door. The Church did not forgive cheaply. It was through hard, public penance.
Cyprian admits the practice. But those bishops did not leave the Church or rebaptise. Novatian’s mistake was not being strict. It was breaking communion over it.

iconoclasm.summary: The Church teaches that images of Christ, Mary and the saints may be made and honoured. The Word became flesh, so he can be seen and painted. The honour given to an image passes to the person it shows. It is respect, never the worship that belongs to God alone.

steps.0: The commandment is real. It aims at idols that take God’s place.
steps.1: The same God ordered carved figures over the mercy seat.
steps.2: The apostles saw and touched the Word made flesh.
steps.3: John of Damascus agrees the Godhead cannot be painted.
steps.4: Nicaea II says images witness that the Incarnation was real.
steps.5: The council separates respect, which passes to the person, from worship, which is God’s alone.
steps.6: The Catechism quotes John of Damascus on the new way of images after the Incarnation.
steps.7: The Church today teaches the same difference.

objections: The council saw this coming. It separated reverence from worship, which is God’s alone. Scripture shows a sign can heal without being worshipped, like the bronze serpent.
Hieria called itself a world council. But Rome and the Eastern patriarchs were not there, and the patriarchs rejected it. Nicaea II had the pope’s legates and Eastern representatives.
No. What is painted is the one Person, the Son who is God and man, as he looked in his humanity. Chalcedon says he is truly man, like us in all things but sin.

monothelitism.summary: The Church teaches, with the Sixth Council, that Christ has two natural wills, divine and human. They are not against each other. The human will freely follows the divine. Without a human will he would not be fully human. “Not my will, but yours” shows both.

steps.0: In Gethsemane Jesus speaks of “my will” and the Father’s will.
steps.1: Jesus again separates his will from the will of the one who sent him.
steps.2: Obedience belongs to a creature’s will. Christ is said to be obedient.
steps.3: Chalcedon says Christ has a complete human nature, with a mind.
steps.4: Leo says the properties of each nature stay in the union.
steps.5: Pope Agatho says Christ had a real human will, without sin.
steps.6: Constantinople III: two wills, working together without division or mixing.
steps.7: Denying a human will would deny a full humanity.
steps.8: The Catechism: the human will freely submits.

objections: Christ’s unity is in the Person, not in the will. One Son wills in a divine way and in a human way. The human will follows the divine, so there is no division.
Salvation is at stake. If the Word had not taken a human will, the part of us that fell by disobedience would not be healed by his obedience.
The council named Honorius. Pope Leo II confirmed it and blamed him for failing to stop the error. The Church makes a difference between that and a solemn teaching.
